notes: Promoted from the official 2015-0772-M packet after local page-boundary inspection. The briefing prepares Clinton for Gore's report on Moscow talks with Yeltsin and Chernomyrdin after Russian objections to the December 1994 NATO expansion process.

title: European Security Architecture, NATO Expansion and Russia
documentType: NSC action memorandum with conceptual paper
sourceNote: Source: Clinton Presidential Records, NSC Cable, Email, and Records Management System, Mandatory Declassification Review 2015-0772-M, Clinton Digital Library PDF pages 116-121. Secret.
notes: Promoted from the official 2015-0772-M packet after local page-boundary inspection. The action memorandum asks Lake and Berger to approve restricted interagency circulation of an NSC conceptual paper written after the Gore Moscow trip, the President's December 21 discussion, the December NAC communique, and Russia's reaction; the attachment sets the 1995 parallel tracks for NATO expansion, a NATO-Russia relationship, PFP, OSCE/CSCE, Ukraine, and CEE consultations.

title: CEEs and Our European Security Policy
sourceNote: Source: Clinton Presidential Records, NSC Cable, Email, and Records Management System, Mandatory Declassification Review 2015-0772-M, Clinton Digital Library PDF pages 127-128. Confidential.
notes: Promoted from the official 2015-0772-M packet after local page-boundary inspection. Fried reports from Central Europe that CEE governments accepted the logic of the Russia-NATO/NATO-enlargement dual track after the Moscow summit, supported Ukraine, treated PFP as a military orientation point, and worried that U.S. public and congressional debate could weaken confidence in the enlargement policy.

title: Troika Meeting on European Security/NATO Enlargement
documentType: NSC information memorandum with strategy papers
sourceNote: Source: Clinton Presidential Records, NSC Cable, Email, and Records Management System, Mandatory Declassification Review 2015-0772-M, Clinton Digital Library PDF pages 131-147. Secret.
notes: Promoted from the official 2015-0772-M packet after local page-boundary inspection. The memorandum and attachments set a 1996 enlargement road map, including the half-step after the December 1995 NAC, pre-accession talks, ratification timing, and a parallel NATO-Russia track.

title: European Security/NATO Enlargement Progress Report
sourceNote: Source: Clinton Presidential Records, NSC Cable, Email, and Records Management System, Mandatory Declassification Review 2015-0772-M, Clinton Digital Library PDF pages 184-187. Secret.
notes: Promoted from the official 2015-0772-M packet after local page-boundary inspection. NSC record ID 9505436; the memo updates the President on the NATO enlargement study, parallel NATO-Russia relationship, CEE anxieties, Russian opposition, congressional strategy, and a possible 1996-1997 accession timetable. Packet pages 159-162, 172-175, and 179-182 contain duplicate or marked copies and are not promoted separately.

title: West European Attitudes Toward NATO Enlargement
sourceNote: Source: Clinton Presidential Records, NSC Cable, Email, and Records Management System, Mandatory Declassification Review 2015-0772-M, Clinton Digital Library PDF pages 169-170. Secret.
notes: Promoted from the official 2015-0772-M packet after local page-boundary inspection. NSC record ID 9505436; Lake answers the President's question about West European attitudes toward NATO enlargement, Russian objections, Baltic membership, EU/NATO sequencing, and allied solidarity. Packet pages 157-158 and 177-178 contain alternate marked copies and are not promoted separately.

title: Inviting Partners to Madrid
sourceNote: Source: Clinton Presidential Records, NSC Cable, Email, and Records Management System, Mandatory Declassification Review 2015-0772-M, Clinton Digital Library PDF pages 389-390. Secret.
notes: Promoted from the official 2015-0772-M packet after local page-boundary inspection. NSC record ID 9702588; Schmidt weighs whether to invite Partnership for Peace partners to Madrid, how to avoid making Russian nonattendance the summit story, and whether an informal NATO-plus-Partners event could preserve an all-European Madrid signal without giving Moscow a de facto veto. Packet page 388 is a routing sheet and is not promoted separately.

title: Strategy and Timelines in the Run-Up to Madrid
documentType: NSC information memorandum with strategy papers
sourceNote: Source: Clinton Presidential Records, NSC Cable, Email, and Records Management System, Mandatory Declassification Review 2015-0772-M, Clinton Digital Library PDF pages 396-414. Secret.
notes: Promoted from the official 2015-0772-M packet after local page-boundary inspection. NSC record ID 9702852; the cover memo forwards a Madrid strategy paper, a chronology, and a key-issues paper then being discussed by Deputies in a restricted setting. The package covers first-round candidates, runners-up, EAPC/APC timing, NATO-Russia charter deadlines, NATO-Ukraine, accession talks, ratification mechanics, ESDI, command structure, and Strategic Concept review. Packet pages 392-395 are withdrawal/RMO/routing controls and are not promoted separately.

title: The NATO-Russia Founding Act
sourceNote: Source: Clinton Presidential Records, NSC Cable, Email, and Records Management System, Mandatory Declassification Review 2015-0772-M, Clinton Digital Library PDF pages 421-422. Confidential.
notes: Promoted from the official 2015-0772-M packet after local page-boundary inspection. The memorandum explains how the Founding Act preserved NATO decision-making while giving Russia a consultative forum during the enlargement process.

title: Deciding Which Countries to Support for NATO Membership at the Madrid Summit
sourceNote: Source: Clinton Presidential Records, NSC Cable, Email, and Records Management System, Mandatory Declassification Review 2015-0772-M, Clinton Digital Library PDF pages 440-447. Secret.
notes: Promoted from the official 2015-0772-M packet after local page-boundary inspection. The action memorandum records the Principals' recommendation that Clinton support Poland, Hungary, and the Czech Republic as the first invitees at Madrid while holding a robust open door.

title: Achieving Allied Consensus on NATO Enlargement: Whether to Set a Date or Name Names for the Second Round
sourceNote: Source: Clinton Presidential Records, NSC Cable, Email, and Records Management System, Mandatory Declassification Review 2015-0772-M, Clinton Digital Library PDF pages 485-492. Confidential.
notes: Promoted from the official 2015-0772-M packet after local page-boundary inspection. The memorandum weighs naming Romania and Slovenia, setting a second-round review date, or preserving the no-names Open Door formula for Madrid.

title: Telephone Conversation with Russian President Yeltsin
sourceNote: Source: Clinton Presidential Records, Meetings and Telephone Calls with Foreign Leaders, Mandatory Declassification Review 2015-0782-M-2, Clinton Library PDF pages 49-51. Confidential.
notes: Promoted from the official 2015-0782-M-2 packet after local page-boundary inspection. In the first Clinton-Yeltsin call after Yeltsin's reelection, Yeltsin says he has spoken with Kohl and Chirac about NATO and believes the sides can find a solution that does not put Clinton in an uncomfortable position, while Clinton points to Gore-Chernomyrdin and Mamedov follow-up. Packet pages 54-56 contain a duplicate marked-up copy and are not promoted separately.

title: Telephone call with President Boris Yeltsin of Russia, February 27, 1997, White House
sourceNote: Source: Clinton Presidential Records, Meetings and Telephone Calls with Foreign Leaders, Mandatory Declassification Review 2015-0782-M-2, Clinton Library PDF pages 87-89. Confidential.
notes: Promoted from the official 2015-0782-M-2 packet after local page-boundary inspection. Yeltsin frames Helsinki as a test of partnership versus Cold War regression, and Clinton previews Talbott's Moscow talks on defining a NATO-Russia relationship alongside NATO enlargement.

title: Helsinki Morning Meeting with President Boris Yeltsin
sourceNote: Source: Clinton Presidential Records, Meetings and Telephone Calls with Foreign Leaders, Mandatory Declassification Review 2015-0782-M-2, Clinton Library PDF pages 105-115. Confidential.
notes: Promoted from the official 2015-0782-M-2 packet after local page-boundary inspection. This is a central enlargement record: Yeltsin asks for an unpublished assurance that no former Soviet republics would enter NATO, while Clinton rejects a secret line and argues for a new NATO, PFP, and a NATO-Russia charter.

title: Helsinki Afternoon Meeting with President Boris Yeltsin
sourceNote: Source: Clinton Presidential Records, Meetings and Telephone Calls with Foreign Leaders, Mandatory Declassification Review 2015-0782-M-2, Clinton Library PDF pages 124-127. Confidential.
notes: Promoted from the official 2015-0782-M-2 packet after local page-boundary inspection. Clinton and Yeltsin coordinate how to describe Russian opposition to enlargement, the NATO-Russia agreement, the absence of a secret deal, and the path toward a pre-Madrid signing.

title: Meeting with President Boris Yeltsin of Russia, May 27, 1997, Paris, France
sourceNote: Source: Clinton Presidential Records, NSC Records Management, Mandatory Declassification Review 2015-0782-M-2, Clinton Library PDF pages 143-150. Confidential; declassified in part.
notes: Promoted from the official 2015-0782-M-2 packet after local page-boundary inspection. The released text follows the Founding Act signing and covers implementation of the NATO-Russia partnership, possible Russian representation at Madrid, the Joint Council, and CFE adaptation.

title: Meeting with President Boris Yeltsin of Russia, June 20, 1997, Denver, Colorado
sourceNote: Source: Clinton Presidential Records, Meetings and Telephone Calls with Foreign Leaders, Mandatory Declassification Review 2015-0782-M-2, Clinton Library PDF pages 165-172. Secret.
notes: Promoted from the official 2015-0782-M-2 packet after local page-boundary inspection. The Denver meeting links the post-Paris NATO-Russia Founding Act to Madrid preparations, CFE adaptation, Russian representation at the NATO summit, and the unresolved mechanics of the Permanent Joint Council.
